NYC helios setup: population, schools and ventilation

This report summarises the New York City inputs used in helios-nyc: the synthetic household population, public school sizes, the population helios generates from them, and the school ventilation assumptions. Charts are static; each has a table with the underlying values.

Key numbers

Measure Value
Households (five boroughs) 3,166,264
People in households 7,847,492
Mean household size 2.48
Public schools (2018-19, open with enrollment) 1,817
Students enrolled 1,065,471
Students per full-time-equivalent teacher 13.5

Sources: households from the RTI synthetic population pipeline (2015-2019 American Community Survey, New York State filtered to the five boroughs, with stochastic rounding of household counts); schools from the NCES Common Core of Data school directory for 2018-19.

Model population

The charts below use a single population generated by helios with the NYC settings (100,000 people). Households and schools are sampled from the data above. Workplace sizes come from helios’s parametric US distribution (an offset truncated power law), not NYC data. Leisure location sizes come from a negative binomial distribution.

School sizes: model population versus NYC data

In the model, school size includes staff. Large schools are drawn rarely in a population of this size, so the model’s upper tail is shorter than the data’s.

Quantile NYC schools (students) Model schools (students and staff)

25% 324 301

75% 682 645
95% 1,347 1,408

School ventilation

Each school’s baseline air changes per hour (ACH) is drawn from a normal distribution truncated at 0. The main analysis uses inputs chosen to reproduce the school-day classroom ACH of 2.0 +/- 1.3 measured by Batterman et al. (2017, Indoor Air, doi:10.1111/ina.12384). The sensitivity scenario enters 2.0 and 1.3 directly.

Scenario Realised mean Realised SD Schools below 0.5 ACH 95th percentile
